changes.text: 1787年9月17日，制宪会议的最后一天。宪法的誊清本宣读完毕，本杰明·富兰克林站起身，手里拿着一份写好的讲稿；麦迪逊的笔记说，他是为了自己方便才把话写下来的，随后由威尔逊代为宣读。会要散了，对桌上这份文件，会上有几位成员公开表示过异议。摆在面前的一个问题是：签不签，怎么签。

September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and Mr. Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Several members openly voiced objections to the document on the table. One question before them: sign it or not, and how.
他给出的同意理由很朴素：他认为“我们需要一个全国政府”。他愿意连同宪法的“全部缺点（如果那算缺点的话）”一起接受它。作者认为，到这里，争的已经不是文本好不好，而是手上有没有更好的东西可拿。

His reason for consenting was down-to-earth: "I think a general government necessary for us." He would take the charter with all its faults, if they were such. In the author's view, by now the argument was not about whether the text was good, but about whether anything better lay within reach.
有保留的人远不止他一个。作者认为，当天的一个核心争点是：签名这件事本身，到底算什么。
Plenty of others had reservations of their own. In the author's view, a central dispute of the day was what the act of signing actually meant.
然后他向仍有异议的成员提出请求：和他一起“稍稍怀疑一下自己的不会出错”，把名字签上去，以“显示我们的一致”。一种解释是，他要的不是人人说好，而是名字出现在同一份文件上。

Then came the request. To any member who still objected he made an appeal: join him in a readiness to "doubt a little of his own infallibility", and put his name to the instrument, "to make manifest our unanimity". One reading: what he asked for was not that everyone praise the document, but that every name appear on the same page.

就在收尾的同一段时间里，会议还在改一个数字。戈勒姆提出，趁还来得及，把“众议员人数不得超过每四万人一名”（该条款曾引起许多讨论）中的四万改为三万，以减少反对意见——这不是绝对规则，只是给国会更大的余地。会议主席（签名栏作乔治·华盛顿，弗吉尼亚代表）起身付表决时说，自己的位置一向使他不就待决问题发表意见，这次却忍不住表示希望通过这项修改，并说许多成员认为代表比例偏小不足以保障人民的权利和利益，他也承认这一直是他自己认为方案中可以挑剔的地方。修改无异议通过，宪法誊清本付签获全体州赞成。

In the same closing stretch the convention was still adjusting a number. Gorham asked, if it was not too late, for the purpose of lessening objections to the Constitution, to reconsider the clause capping representation at one member for every forty thousand people — a clause that had produced so much discussion — and to strike out forty thousand in favour of thirty thousand. That would fix no absolute rule, he remarked, only give Congress greater latitude. When the president rose to put the question — the signature block names him George Washington, deputy from Virginia — he said his office had restrained him from speaking on questions before the House, yet he could not forbear this wish. Many members had thought the small proportion of representatives thin security for the rights and interests of the people; he acknowledged it had always appeared to himself among the exceptionable parts of the plan. The change passed without opposition, and the engrossed Constitution was agreed to for signing, every state answering aye.
伦道夫起身，影射着富兰克林的话，为自己拒签致歉：尽管有压倒多数和德高望重的名字为这份方案背书。他说，拒签不等于他要在会外反对宪法，他只是要保留按日后的判断、照自己的职责行事的自由。

Randolph rose and, alluding to Franklin's observations, apologized for refusing to sign, notwithstanding the vast majority and venerable names that would give the plan their sanction. Refusing, he said, did not mean he would oppose the Constitution outside the convention's doors; he meant only to keep himself free to be governed by his duty, as his future judgment should prescribe it.

接着几位成员各自说明为什么签。莫里斯说，他也有异议，但视此为能得到的最好方案，愿连同缺点照收；多数已经决定，他服从这个决定；方案一出手，其余考虑都会退居其次，问题只剩“要不要有一个全国政府”，否则便是无政府。他并指出，按所提格式签名，只关乎出席各州一致这一事实。汉密尔顿说，他希望人人都签：几个有分量的人若反对甚至拒签，可能点燃潜藏在可能很快消退的拥护热情之下的火星，造成无穷祸害；在无政府与动荡、和方案可能带来的好处之间，没有什么可犹豫的。布朗特说，他本已声明不会以承诺支持的方式签名，但这个格式让他如释重负——他可以不承诺自己，只证明“方案是会议中各州一致的行动”这一事实。

Then several members explained why they would sign. Morris said he had objections, but this was the best that was to be attained, and he would take it with all its faults; the majority had decided and he would abide by that determination. The moment the plan went forth, every other consideration would be laid aside and the great question would be whether there was to be a national government at all — with anarchy as the alternative. The signing in the proposed form, he pointed out, related only to the fact that the states present were unanimous. Hamilton urged that every member sign: a few characters of consequence, by opposing or even refusing, might do infinite mischief, kindling the latent sparks that lurked under an enthusiasm for the convention which might soon subside — and that between anarchy and convulsions and the good the plan might bring there was nothing to hesitate over. Blount said he had declared he would not sign so as to pledge himself to support the plan, but the form relieved him: without committing himself, he could attest the fact that the plan was the unanimous act of the states in convention.

富兰克林随即说明：写那篇讲稿时，他并不知道会有哪位成员拒签，希望大家这样理解；他感谢伦道夫最早提出方案、一路襄助，希望他放下异议，免得他的名字缺席带来大的祸害。伦道夫没有被说动。他说，以这个格式签名，与签宪法本身无异，换形式对他没有区别；拒签可能是他一生中最可怕的一步，但出于良知，他不能犹豫，更不能改变。他还说，把方案以“要么全收、要么全拒”的最终选择交给民众，真正会带来的，正是人们原以为个别人拒签才会招致的无政府和内乱。

Franklin explained that when drawing up that paper he had not known that any particular member would refuse to sign, and hoped to be so understood. He felt a high sense of obligation to Randolph for bringing the plan forward in the first instance and for his help along the way, and hoped he would yet lay aside his objections and prevent the great mischief that the refusal of his name might produce. Randolph was not moved. To sign in the proposed form was, for him, the same as signing the Constitution; the change of form made no difference. Refusing might be the most awful step of his life, but conscience dictated it, and he could not hesitate, much less change. He added that holding out the plan to the people with a final alternative of accepting or rejecting it in toto would really produce the very anarchy and civil convulsions that were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it.
格里接着讲了自己处境的痛苦：他担心眼前的局面会引发内战，尤其在马萨诸塞，那里一派倾向民主——他认为那是最坏的政治祸害——另一派走向相反的极端，两派在反对和抵制宪法中相撞，混乱可忧。格式对他同样无关紧要。但他说，如果别处不会让人知道，拒签的事绝不会由他传出去；他又说，富兰克林的话他只能看作是针对他和其他不签名的人。

Gerry then described the painful feelings of his situation and his fear that the present crisis might end in civil war — in Massachusetts especially, where one party was devoted to democracy, which he thought the worst of all political evils, and the other as violent at the opposite extreme; from the collision of the two, in opposing and resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared. The form meant nothing to him either. But if it were not otherwise apparent, the refusals to sign should never be known from him. As for Franklin's remarks, he said, he could only view them as levelled at himself and the other gentlemen who meant not to sign.
也有人嫌这个格式不够痛快。平克尼认为靠措辞的模糊争取不到多少人，不如坦白，让形式直接说明实质：他自己将以支持宪法的立场签名，也愿意如此承诺。富兰克林答：“在国会和我们的选民认可这份方案之前，就承诺还太早。”英格索尔则给出另一种读法：签名既不只是证明事实，也不是无论如何都要支持，而是“通盘考虑之后，对最可取方案的推荐”。

Others found the form too coy. Pinckney thought ambiguity would win few converts; better to be candid and let the form speak the substance. He meant to sign with a view to supporting the Constitution with all his influence, and would pledge himself accordingly. Franklin replied: "It is too soon to pledge ourselves, before Congress and our constituents shall have approved the plan." Ingersoll offered another reading: the signature was neither a bare attestation of the fact nor a pledge to support the plan at all events, but "a recommendation of what, all things considered, was the most eligible".
另一种解释针对富兰克林请大家“稍稍怀疑一下自己的不会出错”的那句话。作者的引申是：这句话提供的也许不是“方案是对的”这种理由，而是一种在不确定中签字的态度——当另开一次会未必更好时，先承认自己可能错，再把名字放上去。作者提出的替代选择是要求在签名旁写明保留意见；但作者同样承认，那样做会削弱“一致”的分量，而那正是当天有人力求的东西。

A second reading turns on Franklin's plea to "doubt a little of his own infallibility". The author's extension, not Franklin's words: what he offered may have been less a reason to call the plan right than a posture for signing under uncertainty. When another convention might well do no better, first admit you may be wrong, then put your name down. The author's alternative would be to require a written reservation beside each signature, but the author also grants that this would weaken the unanimity some in the room were pressing for that day.
现代虚构场景一：一个评审委员会刚刚否决了一位同事力推的方案。散会后，有成员在走廊里跟人说，自己其实也不同意，只是被多数压了下来。另一种做法是：在会议室里把反对讲透，出了门就不再外传已经结束的分歧。这不是隐瞒结果，而是不在外面把同一场仗再打一遍。

Fictional modern scene one. A review committee has just turned down a plan that one colleague pushed hard for. Afterwards a member tells someone in the corridor that they had disagreed too and were simply outvoted. Another way is possible: argue the objection fully in the room, then stop spreading a settled disagreement once you are outside. That is not hiding the outcome; it is declining to fight the same battle again in the hallway.
这场会议的记录主要来自詹姆斯·麦迪逊的笔记，后收入1845年埃利奥特编本（维基文库）。1793年出版的《富兰克林文集》收有这篇讲稿的印本（题作 Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention），可以拿来对照，但本篇没有逐字比对两版。正文的英文引语都取自麦迪逊笔记一版；富兰克林讲稿的措辞在两版间是否有出入，本篇不作断言。

The meeting is known chiefly from James Madison's notes, printed in Elliot's 1845 edition (Wikisource). The 1793 Works of Franklin carries a printed text of the speech under the title "Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention", which can be set beside it, but this piece has not collated the two word by word. All English quotations in the body of the piece are taken from Madison's notes; whether the wording of Franklin's speech differs between the two versions is not asserted.

记录本身的来路也值得留意。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议记录或交主席保管，理由是记录若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把记录交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

The record's own provenance deserves a look. In these notes King suggests that the journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.
会场记录主要来自麦迪逊的笔记（1845年埃利奥特编本，维基文库）；1793年《富兰克林文集》所印讲稿可作对照，本篇未逐字比对两版。英文引语均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段，人物发言按笔记转述，未替任何人补写动机或心理；作者的推断均已标明为解释。

The record comes chiefly from Madison's notes (Elliot's 1845 edition, Wikisource); the speech as printed in the 1793 Works of Franklin can serve as a check, and the two have not been collated word by word here. All English quotations are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes; speeches are reported as the notes give them, no motive or psychology has been supplied for anyone, and the author's inferences are marked as interpretation.
